interfaces: ContextRole = Developer | QA | Architect | UAT/Product | MergeController
ContextCompileInput { role, task, registry, revision, artifacts }
ContextPackage { schemaVersion, role, taskId, sourceRevision, task, artifacts, manifest }

behavioralConstraints: Developer receives implementation-local task scope requirements direct dependency context relevant contracts and local fixtures/scenarios
QA receives requirements acceptance/validation context exact-revision diff relevant local contracts fixtures/scenarios and revision-bound evidence but excludes developer narrative as authority
Architect receives affected and direct-dependency contracts exact-revision diff/evidence architecture policy and downstream consumer semantics
UAT/Product receives outcome-focused task fields local scenarios and QA/Architecture evidence without broad implementation detail
MergeController receives task/branch/review-role identity policy and exact-revision evidence facts without broad implementation detail
Developer QA and Architect fail explicitly when referenced requirement or required relevant contract artifacts are missing
QA and Architect fail explicitly when an exact-revision diff is missing
equivalent input snapshots produce equivalent package content and artifact ordering regardless of artifact input order
invariants: compiler is read-only and does not mutate lifecycle assignment lock or branch state
compiler invokes no agent provider and performs no review judgment
non-Developer roles exclude artifacts marked developer-narrative authority
Architect context is intentionally broader than Developer and QA for semantic consumer compatibility
every package identifies its exact source revision and every included artifact
examples: Architect derives consumer-requirement artifacts from knownConsumers in affected module contracts while Developer omits them
QA includes deterministic Developer validation evidence for the exact revision but excludes developer narrative justification
recompiling Architect with the same artifact set in reverse input order yields an equivalent package
edgeCases: missing direct dependency task fails for Developer and Architect
wrong-revision diff cannot satisfy QA or Architect compilation
empty or whitespace-padded revision identity is rejected
contract without parseable knownConsumers remains usable without derived consumer artifacts

expectations: Developer packages remain local and deterministic
required missing artifacts fail explicitly instead of silently reducing context
acceptedRanges: Developer ContextPackage for any valid task and exact revision
requiredReachableRanges: Developer package with task requirement direct dependency contract fixture and scenario context

expectations: QA Architect and UAT/Product receive intentionally different context
Architect can inspect downstream consumer semantic expectations and ranges
QA never treats developer narrative self-justification as authority
acceptedRanges: QA Architect and UAT/Product ContextPackage variants

expectations: MergeController context remains facts-only and exact-revision bound
requiredReachableRanges: task identity canonical branch required review roles policy and exact-revision evidence
